advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the unreachable trailing hand_back/return (or restructure so exactly one hand-back path exists) in drive_to_submit.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:234-236: internal guard `if wip.re_drive_count >= MAX_RE_DRIVE:` returns 'handed_back'
re_drive_count increments once per iteration (line 242); by the 6th iteration count==5==MAX_RE_DRIVE so the guard always returns before loop exhaustion, leaving lines 244-245 dead
advisory.finding: The trailing `hand_back(...)` and `return "handed_back"` after the `for` loop in `drive_to_submit` are unreachable: the in-loop guard `if wip.re_drive_count >= MAX_RE_DRIVE` always fires and returns by the final iteration, so the loop never exits normally to reach lines 244-245.
scenarios: Future maintainer changes the loop bound or guard and is misled by the duplicated tail path
advisory.suggested_fix: Iterate `range(MAX_RE_DRIVE)` and keep the post-loop hand_back as the single exhaustion path, or drop the redundant tail and keep only the in-loop guard.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a FakeTransport boundary test for `GerritClient.set_review` asserting the `/revisions/current/review` path and that the body includes only the provided `message`/`labels`.
evidence: tests/autolander/test_s2a_routing_held_out.py:125-131 establishes the boundary-test norm: `test_rebase_posts_on_behalf_of_uploader_body` asserts `path.endswith('/rebase')` and `body == {...}` via FakeTransport
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `set_review` in tests finds only assertions against `RecordingClient.calls` (the fake at _autolander_fakes.py:87) and no FakeTransport route for the review endpoint
advisory.finding: The new `GerritClient.set_review` method has no HTTP-boundary test asserting its request path and body, unlike its siblings `rebase`/`rebase_chain`/`query_changes` which each have a FakeTransport routing test. A regression in the endpoint string `/revisions/current/review` or in the None-skipping body construction (omitting `message`/`labels` when unset) would ship undetected — all hand_back tests use the fake `RecordingClient.set_review`, which never exercises the real wire code.
scenarios: A typo in the review endpoint path or dropping the None-guard on `message`/`labels`
Gerrit rejecting a malformed review body at runtime
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring `test_rebase_posts_on_behalf_of_uploader_body`: route `POST /revisions/current/review`, call `client.set_review('123', message='m', labels={'Autosubmit': 0})`, and assert the recorded path ends with `/revisions/current/review` and `body == {'message': 'm', 'labels': {'Autosubmit': 0}}`; add a second case with only `labels` to assert `message` is omitted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `hand_back` test with a non-default `reason` asserting the emitted comment uses the `handed back: <reason>` form.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:195: `comment = HANDBACK_COMMENT if reason == HANDBACK_NEEDS_REBASE else f"handed back: {reason}"`
test_s2b_drive_held_out.py:130 calls `hand_back(client, wip, record_handback=...)` with default reason; test_exhaustion_hands_back passes `HANDBACK_NEEDS_REBASE`
ABSENCE: no test passes a non-default `reason` to `hand_back`
advisory.finding: The `hand_back` comment ternary's non-default branch (`else f"handed back: {reason}"`) is never exercised — every `hand_back` invocation in tests uses the default `HANDBACK_NEEDS_REBASE` reason, so a regression in the non-default reason's comment text would not be caught.
scenarios: S3 reuses hand_back for a conflict/CI-fail reason other than needs_rebase
